region.en: Nina and the marsh lagoon, Iraq
region.zh: 妮娜與沼澤潟湖（伊拉克）

texts.period: Old Babylonian manuscript, c. 1700 BCE (ETCSL translation 2003)

source.work: A hymn to Nanshe (Nanshe A, ETCSL c.4.14.1)

texts.license: ETCSL translation (Oxford, 2003-2006); quoted in paraphrase with attribution

summary.en: The daughter of Enki is praised as lady of fish and birds, interpreter of dreams and patron of the orphan: on New Year's day she judges the land, weighing the widow's case — the goddess of social justice and the lagoon's wealth.
summary.zh: 恩基之女被頌為魚鳥之主、解夢之師、孤兒之護：新年之日她審理天下，為寡婦秉公裁斷——兼具社會正義與湖沼財富的女神。

sensitivity.note: Ancient hymn; no living community restrictions.

passages.text: Nanshe, daughter of Enki, is praised as lady of the fish and the birds of the lagoon, whose own mother was born of the water's plenty.
passages.note: Paraphrase of ETCSL c.4.14.1, opening praise; not verbatim.

passages.text: She is the interpreter of dreams and the patron of the orphan and the widow: on New Year's day she holds court, weighing the cases of the poor with the water's justice.
passages.note: Paraphrase of ETCSL c.4.14.1, the New Year court; not verbatim.

functions: Charter of the marsh administration and its justice

variants.name: Nanshe and the birds
variants.summary: The narrative companion of the hymn.

secondary_sources.citation: Thorkild Jacobsen, New Haven, 1976, on Nanshe

texts.period: Old Babylonian manuscript, c. 1700 BCE (ETCSL translation 2003)

source.work: Nanshe and the birds (Nanshe C, ETCSL c.4.14.3)

texts.license: ETCSL translation (Oxford, 2003-2006); quoted in paraphrase with attribution

summary.en: The birds of the marsh dispute their stations before their mistress; each is named, its cry described and its place assigned — a comic catalogue of the lagoon's citizens judged by the goddess.
summary.zh: 沼澤群鳥於女主之前爭論職位；逐一具名、摹其啼聲、各定其位——潟湖公民的喜劇目錄，由女神親裁。

sensitivity.note: Ancient hymn; no living community restrictions.

passages.text: The birds of the marsh come before their mistress Nanshe to dispute their stations; each is named, its cry described, its feathers and habits catalogued — a comic assembly of the lagoon's citizens.
passages.note: Paraphrase of ETCSL c.4.14.3, the assembly; not verbatim.

passages.text: The goddess assigns each bird its place, and the dispute is settled with her own wit — the marsh given its constitution in verse.
passages.note: Paraphrase of ETCSL c.4.14.3, the settlement; not verbatim.

functions: Comic catalogue of the marsh's birds

variants.name: The debate between Bird and Fish

title.en: Nisaba, the Grain and the Stylus

texts.period: Old Babylonian manuscript, c. 1700 BCE (ETCSL translation 2003)

source.work: A hymn to Nisaba (Nisaba A, ETCSL c.4.16.1)

texts.license: ETCSL translation (Oxford, 2003-2006); quoted in paraphrase with attribution

summary.en: The goddess of grain is praised as the scribe of the gods: she who measures the harvest on her lapis tablet, who lends her name to every school exercise — the patron of the writing that makes order.
summary.zh: 穀物女神被頌為眾神之書記：於青金石泥板上量度收成，以其名冠於每份校習之卷——使秩序得以成立的書寫之守護者。

sensitivity.note: Ancient hymn; no living community restrictions.

passages.text: Nisaba is praised as the grain goddess and the scribe of the gods: the one who measures the harvest on her lapis tablet and counts the years.
passages.note: Paraphrase of ETCSL c.4.16.1, opening praise; not verbatim.

passages.text: She lends her name to every school exercise, and the closing prayer asks her for the art of writing perfected — the patroness of the craft that makes order out of accounts.
passages.note: Paraphrase of ETCSL c.4.16.1, the school prayer; not verbatim.

functions: Patroness liturgy of the scribal schools
Theology of accounting as divine order

variants.name: A sir-namsub to Nisaba (Nisaba B)
variants.summary: The companion hymn of the goddess.

secondary_sources.work: Gods, Demons and Symbols of Ancient Mesopotamia
secondary_sources.citation: Jeremy Black and Anthony Green, London, 1992, entry 'Nisaba'

title.en: Ninlil, Lady of the Grain-Filled City

texts.period: Old Babylonian manuscript, c. 1700 BCE (ETCSL translation 2003)

source.work: An adab to Ninlil (Ninlil A, ETCSL c.4.24.1)

texts.license: ETCSL translation (Oxford, 2003-2006); quoted in paraphrase with attribution

summary.en: Enlil's consort is praised as the lady whose presence fills the granaries: the queen of Nippur whose word with her lord's decides the year — the adab hymn of the city's mother.
summary.zh: 恩利爾之妻被頌為使倉廩充盈之女主：尼普魯王后，其言與其主之命共同裁決歲事——城邦之母的阿達卜頌詩。

sensitivity.note: Ancient hymn; no living community restrictions.

passages.text: Ninlil is praised as the lady whose presence fills the granaries: the queen of Nippur, whose word with her lord's decides the year's plenty.
passages.note: Paraphrase of ETCSL c.4.24.1, the praise; not verbatim.

passages.text: The adab's refrain asks her intercession: through the lady, the lord's anger is softened — the queen as the land's advocate before the storm god.
passages.note: Paraphrase of ETCSL c.4.24.1, the refrain; not verbatim.

variants.name: Enlil and Sud
variants.summary: The marriage myth of the same couple.

region.zh: 尼普魯書吏學校（伊拉克）

texts.period: Old Babylonian proverb collections, c. 1700 BCE (ETCSL translation 2003)
texts.license: ETCSL translation (Oxford, 2003-2006); quoted in paraphrase with attribution

summary.en: In the proverb collections the fox is the sly one: he who set a snare for others is caught in his own — the school texts' fox tales teaching wit's price, the ancestor of the trickster fable.
summary.zh: 諺語集中狐狸為狡黠者：為他人設阱者自陷其中——校中狐語教導機智的代價，為騙徒寓言之源。

sensitivity.note: Ancient proverb literature; no living community restrictions.

passages.text: In the proverb collections the fox is the sly one: the fox who set a snare for others is caught in his own — the collections' repeated moral on cunning's price.
passages.note: Paraphrase of the proverb collections (ETCSL c.6.1-6.2), fox proverbs; not verbatim.

passages.text: The school texts used the fox tales to teach scribal wit and its limits: the animal fable teaching what the debate poems argued — the ancestor of the trickster fable in world literature.
passages.note: Paraphrase of the proverb collections; not verbatim.

functions: School proverbs on cunning and its price
Ancestor of the trickster fable tradition

variants.name: The heron and the turtle
variants.summary: The animal fable of the same wisdom.

title.en: A Hymn to Suen for the Last King

region.en: Ur, at the empire's fall, Iraq
region.zh: 烏爾，帝國傾覆之際（伊拉克）

texts.period: Ur III composition, c. 2000 BCE (ETCSL translation 2003)

source.work: A tigi to Suen for Ibbi-Suen (Ibbi-Suen A, ETCSL c.2.4.5.1)

texts.license: ETCSL translation (Oxford, 2003-2006); quoted in paraphrase with attribution

summary.en: The last king of Ur is hymned by his moon god's cult even as the empire crumbles: the tigi song for Ibbi-Suen praises Suen and prays for the city — the liturgy sung at the edge of the fall that the laments will mourn.
summary.zh: 帝國傾覆之際，烏爾月神祭團仍頌末代之王：伊比辛的提吉頌歌讚美蘇恩、為城祈禱——哀歌所悼之敗亡邊緣所唱之禮樂。

sensitivity.note: Ancient royal hymn; no living community restrictions.

passages.text: The tigi song for Ibbi-Suen praises Suen, the moon god, and prays for the city his cult still serves — the liturgy sung at the edge of the fall.
passages.note: Paraphrase of ETCSL c.2.4.5.1, the hymn; not verbatim.

passages.text: The king is named the god's shepherd even as the provinces slip away — the last royal hymn of Ur, sung before the laments for the city took over the genre.
passages.note: Paraphrase of ETCSL c.2.4.5.1; not verbatim.

functions: Last royal hymn of the Ur III dynasty
Liturgical bridge to the city-lament genre

variants.name: The lament for Urim
variants.summary: The lament that followed the fall.

primary_sources.work: A tigi to Suen for Ibbi-Suen

title.en: Ninisina, the Doctor of the Gods

texts.period: Old Babylonian manuscript, c. 1700 BCE (ETCSL translation 2003)
texts.license: ETCSL translation (Oxford, 2003-2006); quoted in paraphrase with attribution

summary.en: The healing goddess of Isin is praised as the doctor of the gods: she who knows the herb and the incantation, whose hands bind the wound — the liturgy of medicine as divine craft.
summary.zh: 伊辛療癒女神被頌為眾神之醫：通曉藥草與咒文、親手裹傷者——以醫術為神藝之禮讚。

sensitivity.note: Ancient hymn; no living community restrictions.

passages.text: Ninisina is praised as the doctor of the gods: she who knows the herb and the incantation, whose hands bind the wound and cool the fever.
passages.note: Paraphrase of the Ninisina hymns (ETCSL c.4.22), opening praise; not verbatim.

passages.text: The hymn's liturgy asks the goddess's craft for the sick of the city: medicine as divine gift, the healer the gods' own surgeon — the theology of Mesopotamian medical practice.
passages.note: Paraphrase of the Ninisina hymns; not verbatim.

functions: Liturgy of the healing cult at Isin
Theology of medicine as divine craft

secondary_sources.work: Gods, Demons and Symbols of Ancient Mesopotamia
secondary_sources.citation: Jeremy Black and Anthony Green, London, 1992, entry 'Ninisina'

title.zh: 阿薩爾盧希：馬爾杜克的蘇美名

texts.period: Old Babylonian manuscript, c. 1700 BCE (ETCSL translation 2003)
texts.license: ETCSL translation (Oxford, 2003-2006); quoted in paraphrase with attribution

summary.en: Before Babylon's god was Marduk he was Asarluhi of Kuara: the Sumerian hymns praise the exorcist's god — the mace that talks, the wise man's helper — whose name Enuma Elish would give to Marduk as his first of fifty.
summary.zh: 巴比倫之神未稱馬爾杜克前，本是庫阿拉的阿薩爾盧希：蘇美頌詩讚其為驅邪師之神——會說話的神杖、智者的助力——其名後成馬爾杜克五十名號之首。

sensitivity.note: Ancient hymn; no living community restrictions.

passages.text: Before Babylon's god was Marduk he was Asarluhi of Kuara: the Sumerian hymns praise the exorcist's god, the mace that talks, the wise man's helper.
passages.note: Paraphrase of the Asarluhi hymns (ETCSL c.4.01), opening praise; not verbatim.

passages.text: Enuma Elish would give his name to Marduk as the first of the fifty: the old god absorbed by the new — the theological engineering of Babylon's rise, already visible in the Sumerian liturgy.
passages.note: Paraphrase of the hymns; not verbatim.

functions: Sumerian liturgy of the god later absorbed by Marduk
Document of the theological synthesis behind Enuma Elish

variants.name: Enuma Elish: the fifty names
variants.summary: The name of Asarluhi as Marduk's first title.

texts.period: Old Babylonian manuscript, c. 1700 BCE (ETCSL translation 2003)
texts.license: ETCSL translation (Oxford, 2003-2006); quoted in paraphrase with attribution

summary.en: The herald of the gods is praised as the bringer of justice to the land: the god who walks ahead of the judgment, whose lamp is the truth — the theology of the fair hearing in Lagash's liturgy.
summary.zh: 眾神信使被頌為帶來正義者：行於審判之前、以真理為燈之神——拉加什祭儀中的公正聽審神學。

sensitivity.note: Ancient hymn; no living community restrictions.

passages.text: Hendursaga is praised as the herald of the gods who brings justice to the land: the god who walks ahead of the judgment, whose lamp is the truth.
passages.note: Paraphrase of the Hendursaga hymns (ETCSL c.4.06), opening praise; not verbatim.

passages.text: The hymn's liturgy asks the herald for the fair hearing: the small man's case heard as the great man's — the theology of justice in Lagash's cult.
passages.note: Paraphrase of the hymns; not verbatim.

functions: Justice theology of the Lagash temple state
